text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Namibia's ruling party, Swapo, does not have a proper list of its own members and admits being "administratively and technically weak".

- Swapo-owned businesses are worth an estimated N$150 million and are expected to escalate in value to N$250 million by the end of March 1998, according to a central committee report tabled at the party's congress at the weekend.

- Namibia still imports most of its pork from South Africa, although the country itself produces about 15,000 tonnes of pork annually with 18,000 tonnes of caracasses and processed pork, as well as 15,000 live animals imported from South Africa.

- The continuing political discord at Rehoboth against the government-recognised traditional leader of the area, Kaptein Hans Diergaardt, could lead to the loss of foreign investment of N$60 million for the community striving for development.
